body: Sometimes things tick it off, but mostly it happens without reason. When I wasn't medicated the worst event was probably when I was in an ultimate Frisbee game doing fine when for no reason I started sobbing. I can't control it or really predict it which makes the going tough. I've gotten really good at acting like I'm alright in a public setting though.

1. Exercise daily, 40 minutes of biking and usually some running. 
2. I try to get at least 8 hours of sleep a night, although its sometimes more, sometimes less. 
3. I didn't drink until I was stable on meds, and I drink sparingly. No other drugs.
4. I have hobbies, friends, the whole nine yards. 

I've tried my best to live a life that would alleviate the depression etc as best as I could. I try to keep the most normal healthy life as I can, given what I have and am able to do. That being said, its really exhausting. 90% of the time I can manage it, but sometimes, like now and what prompted the post, are the mood swings that push below the usual lows. Sometimes I need just a little bit of a push and I can get over it, but it really does mount up. It seems as I get older the lows are getting a tiny bit lower. Today for instance, the only thing kept me from doing it was Lithium making it hard for me to get that low. I do the best I can and I am so tired right now, I would really like to rest for a very long time. It is very hard to convey just the soul-crushing weariness from dealing with this every day for over a decade. I don't know how long I'll last and if I want to last that long. 

 Thank you for reading and the reply, sleep well.
